focus: P3 advertised golden-scenario versus actual event-shape and intermediate/final-state oracle audit
noveltyJustification: The orientation already identified two nominal fixtures; this complete ten-case audit adds the nogood and timeout contradictions, distinguishes final snapshots from self-referential intermediate replay checks, defines the paired operation-outcome/event/checkpoint transcript, and gives exact assertion and negative-control shapes for 036 cross-adapter parity.
keyFindings: Golden coverage must validate semantic event patterns and required fields rather than fixture filenames
Committed external prefix checkpoints are required because fold versus fold-up-to can share the same reducer defect
Refusals require a paired operation-outcome transcript proving exact refusal shape and zero domain mutation
Claim-lease, nogood, out-of-order, and human-timeout fixtures do not prove their full advertised scenarios
Cross-adapter parity must compare ordered operation outcomes, accepted event envelopes, and projection checkpoints
Every parity scenario needs a plausible-wrong mutant that fails with the expected divergence class and earliest mismatch

ruledOut.approach: Treat required fixture filenames as mechanism coverage
ruledOut.reason: Names do not prove required event kinds, fields, refusals, or state transitions

ruledOut.approach: Use final-state equality as behavioral parity
ruledOut.reason: Terminal-equal paths can differ in denials, effects, budgets, retries, and unsafe intermediate states

ruledOut.approach: Treat fold versus fold-up-to equality as an external intermediate oracle
ruledOut.reason: Both computations can share the same reducer defect

ruledOut.approach: Represent refused operations as domain events
ruledOut.reason: Refusals are operation outcomes and must prove the domain ledger and projection remained unchanged

ruledOut.approach: Normalize away all adapter trace differences
ruledOut.reason: Actor, causality, refusal, effect, budget, and transition fields are load-bearing semantic observations

nextFocus: P3 negative controls, intermediate-state assertions, and cross-adapter traces
